# Unicamp está entre 20% das melhores universidades do mundo, aponta o ranking THE - Notícias

![A universidade sobressaiu-se principalmente nas áreas de Educação e Ambiente de Pesquisa, dois dos cinco grandes pilares analisados pela THE](https://jornal.unicamp.br/wp-content/uploads/sites/32/2024/10/Ju_20241009_-Ranking_THE_Pedro_Amatuzzi_mosaico.jpg)A universidade sobressaiu-se principalmente nas áreas de Educação e Ambiente de Pesquisa, dois dos cinco grandes pilares analisados pela THE

Segunda melhor universidade do Brasil, a Unicamp figura entre as 20% melhores do planeta, aponta o *World University Rankings 2025*. Publicado nesta quarta-feira (9), o ranking é elaborado pela *Times Higher Education* (THE, na sigla em inglês), uma das instituições pioneiras na avaliação acadêmica. Para a lista, foram analisadas 2092 universidades de 115 países. Pela primeira vez desde o lançamento do ranking, em 2004, o Brasil figura entre os 20 países mais bem colocados. A Universidade de Oxford (Reino Unido) encabeça a classificação geral, sendo considerada a melhor do mundo. Entre as brasileiras, a Universidade de São Paulo (USP) conquistou a primeira posição.

O *THE World University Rankings 2025* mostra a evolução da Unicamp nos últimos anos. A Universidade, que aparece entre a 351ª e a 400ª posição na classificação geral, sobressaiu-se principalmente nas áreas de Educação e Ambiente de Pesquisa, dois dos cinco grandes pilares analisados pela *Times Higher Education* – os demais são Qualidade de Pesquisa; Indústria; e Perspectiva Internacional. Para conferir a pontuação de cada universidade, são considerados 18 indicadores de desempenho, distribuídos nessas grandes áreas.

“Importante destacar que a Unicamp vem galgando posições nas avaliações dos rankings, seja na classificação geral a nível mundial, passando no THE de uma posição situada entre 401 e 500 para uma entre 351 e 400 nas últimas duas avaliações e mantendo a segunda colocação a nível nacional”, disse o reitor da Unicamp Antonio José de Almeida Meirelles.

“Vale ainda observar que nosso desempenho foi muito bom em ensino e em ambiente de pesquisa, com posições mais próximas ao topo da classificação, indicando que estamos trilhando o caminho certo em termos da combinação destes dois pilares da avaliação,” acrescentou ele.

“Os pilares Educação e Ambiente de Pesquisa representam quase 60% do ranking. Em ensino, a Unicamp teve uma colocação bastante destacada, na classificação geral, ficando na 141ª posição. Em relação ao ambiente de pesquisa, ficou em 168º lugar. Esses indicadores mantêm a Universidade em uma posição considerada elevada, em relação ao restante do mundo”, afirma Renato Garcia, professor do Instituto de Economia (IE) da Universidade e assessor da Pró-Reitoria de Desenvolvimento Universitário.

![O assessor da Pró-Reitoria de Desenvolvimento Universitário, Renato Garcia: posição considerada elevada](https://jornal.unicamp.br/wp-content/uploads/sites/32/2024/10/Ju_20241009_-Ranking_THE_scarpa_AJS_2484-Capa.jpg)O assessor da Pró-Reitoria de Desenvolvimento Universitário, Renato Garcia: posição considerada elevada

No que diz respeito a indústrias e patentes, o desempenho da Unicamp também se sobressaiu, contabilizando 76,7 pontos, completa o docente. O desempenho da Universidade se destaca, sobretudo, quando se leva em conta o aumento no número de participantes, explica Garcia. Em relação à versão anterior, 185 novas instituições foram incluídas no ranking atual. Somente no Brasil, foram mais de 60 universidades.

Para a produção da edição 2025 do ranking, a THE considerou mais de 157 milhões de citações, em 18 milhões de publicações. Também incluiu respostas de mais de 93 mil acadêmicos de diversos países do mundo. O ambiente de ensino, o volume, a receita e a reputação do ambiente de pesquisa estão entre os pontos analisados nas duas categorias em que a Unicamp teve seus melhores resultados.

**Leia mais:**

[Unicamp é a 3ª melhor da América Latina pelo 2º ano consecutivo](https://jornal.unicamp.br/noticias/2024/10/03/unicamp-e-3a-na-america-latina-pelo-2o-ano-consecutivo/)

Discover the top universities for sustainability with the *Times Higher Education* Impact Rankings 2025, which ranks 2,526 universities from 130 countries or territories based on their progress towards the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

## **University sustainability rankings 2025: key insights**

- **Western Sydney University** in Australia is number one overall for fourth consecutive year
- **Indonesia**’s Universitas Airlangga, in joint ninth place, is most sustainable institution from an emerging economy
- **Asian universities** claim more than half of all places in the rankings, and 10 out of the 17 individual SDG rankings are now led by an Asian university
- **Eight countries/territories** make their debut in the sustainability rankings this year: Botswana, Burkina Faso, El Salvador, Estonia, Maldives, Namibia, Papua New Guinea and Senegal

The overall Impact Rankings tableidentifies and celebrates universities that demonstrate comprehensive excellence in contributing to global sustainable development. By excelling in a variety of SDGs, these universities showcase their commitment to addressing the world’s most pressing challenges, including environmental sustainability, social inclusion, economic growth and partnerships.

## World Ranking

### USP Achieves Prestigious Global Recognition in UI GreenMetric World University Rankings (2026)

We are proud to announce that the University of Southern Punjab (USP) has once again secured its place in the UI GreenMetric World University Rankings 2026, earning recognition among the world’s leading sustainable universities.  
In the 2026 rankings, USP has been ranked 455th globally, 15th among universities in Pakistan, and 8th among private-sector universities nationwide. Notably, USP has secured the #1 position among private universities in South Punjab, reaffirming its commitment to sustainability and environmental responsibility.  
This remarkable achievement reflects USP’s continued efforts in promoting eco-friendly infrastructure, energy efficiency, effective waste management, sustainable transportation, and the integration of sustainability into education and research.  
The recognition represents another significant milestone in USP’s journey toward building a greener, more sustainable, and environmentally responsible future.

![](https://usp.edu.pk/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/USP-Green-Metric-Logo-2026-1024x1024.png)

### USP Achieves Prestigious Global Recognition in UI GreenMetric World University Rankings (2025)

We are proud to share that the **University of Southern Punjab (USP)** has once again secured its position in the **UI GreenMetric World University Rankings 2025**, earning recognition among the **top sustainable universities worldwide**. USP is ranked **490th globally**, **16th among all universities in Pakistan**, and **9th in the private sector nationwide**. Notably, USP stands **#1 among Private Universities in South Punjab**, reaffirming its leadership in sustainability and environmental responsibility. This achievement reflects USP’s continued focus on eco-friendly infrastructure, efficient energy use, waste management, sustainable transportation, and strong integration of sustainability into education and research. It’s a clear step forward in our long-term vision for a greener and more responsible future.

![](https://usp.edu.pk/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/USP-Green-Metric-2025-1024x1024.png)

### USP Achieves Prestigious Global Recognition in UI GreenMetric World University Rankings (2024)

We are proud to announce that the **University of Southern Punjab (USP)** has earned a place among the **Top 400 Universities in the World** according to the **UI GreenMetric World University Rankings**!

This remarkable achievement highlights our commitment to sustainability, innovation, and academic excellence.

- **1st in Private Sector Universities of South Punjab**
- **13th Among All Universities in Pakistan**

The UI GreenMetric ranking evaluates universities across the globe based on their environmental sustainability efforts, infrastructure, energy usage, waste management, transportation, education, and research. # Office of International Relations

## [UFSC stands out in the Times Higher Education (THE) Impact Rankings 2025](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2025/06/18/ufsc-se-destaca-na-times-higher-education-the-impact-rankings-2025/?lang=en)

![THE's Impact Rankings 2025 Masterclass | Times Higher Education (THE)](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/sites/default/files/impact-ranking-2025.png)The Times Higher Education (THE) published today, 18 June, the [Impact Rankings 2025](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/impactrankings), which ranks **2,526 universities** from 130 countries or territories based on their progress towards the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

In the overall ranking, [UFSC is placed in the **601–800** range](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/universidade-federal-de-santa-catarina), with a score of 66.4. Regarding the SDGs, the university performed best in the following areas:

- **SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-Being:** ranked 201-300 overall, among 1,788 universities assessed, with a score of 66.4;
- **SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy:** ranked 201-300 overall, among 1,181 universities assessed, with a score of 58.2;
- **SDG 17 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions (SDG 16):** ranked 301-400 overall, among 1,256 institutions assessed, with a score of 59.1.

UFSC also stood out in SDG 6 (Clean water and sanitation), SGD 9 (Industry, innovation and infrastructure), and SDG 12 (Responsible consumption and production).

**About THE and the Impact Rankings**

Times Higher Education (THE) is a British magazine that publishes news and articles on higher education and annually produces a set of rankings considered among the most comprehensive, balanced and reliable in the world. In addition to the institutional actions related to the SDGs, THE also ranks institutions based on the research conducted for each goal.

The *Impact Rankings* specifically highlight universities that stand out in relation to the United Nations SDGs, not only in individual areas but also in their overall contribution to sustainable global development. By excelling in a variety of SDGs, these universities showcase their commitment to addressing the world’s most pressing challenges, including environmental sustainability, social inclusion and economic growth.

For more information, visit the website: [www.timeshighereducation.com/impactrankings](http://www.timeshighereducation.com/impactrankings)

[See the digital edition of the Impact Rankings 2025](https://flipbooks.timeshighereducation.com/19712/133198/index.html?70845)

## [UFSC ranks among the top 5 most sustainable universities in Brazil according to QS Sustainability Rankings 2025](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2024/12/10/ufsc-esta-entre-as-5-universidades-brasileiras-mais-sustentaveis-de-acordo-com-o-qs-world-university-rankings-sustainability-2025/?lang=en)

![](http://sinter.paginas.ufsc.br/files/2024/12/ranking-Qs.jpg)The Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) has been ranked 5th among the most sustainable universities in Brazil in the **QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2025**. The ranking evaluates higher education institutions worldwide based on three key categories: environmental impact, social impact, and governance.

UFSC excelled particularly in the **Environmental Education** and **Environmental Research** lenses, highlighting its dedication to sustainability and the preparation of professionals committed to environmental preservation. Additionally, the University performed notably in the **Equality** and **Health and Wellbeing** lenses, underscoring its commitment to fostering social values ​​through academic and institutional practices.

The 2025 rankings evaluated 1,744 universities, marking a 25% increase from the previous year’s 1,397 universities. Among Brazilian universities, participation grew by 23.5%, rising from 34 institutions in the previous year to 42 in 2025.

While the methodology underwent minor adjustments in specific indicators, the performance lenses, indicators, and weightings remained consistent with the previous year.

The QS Sustainability Rankings are globally recognized for highlighting institutions that integrate sustainable practices into their activities and curricula. UFSC’s achievement reinforces its international relevance in higher education and its leadership in promoting a sustainable future.

To view the full ranking, visit the [official QS page](https://www.topuniversities.com/sustainability-rankings).

## [UFSC is among the 4 best institutions in Brazil according to the THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2025](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2024/11/22/ufsc-esta-entre-as-4-melhores-instituicoes-do-brasil-no-interdisciplinary-science-rankings-2025-do-the/?lang=en)

The Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) achieved the 4th position among the best universities in Brazil in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2025. The ranking, which is in its first edition, measures the contribution and commitment of global universities to interdisciplinary science.

The Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2025 evaluated 749 universities from 92 countries and is currently led by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. In the overall ranking, UFSC is in the 136th position. As for Brazil, the leading institution is the Universidade de São Paulo (USP).

The ranking is based on 11 indicators evaluating institutions in three main areas, each representing a stage in the life cycle of research projects: Inputs (funding); Process (measures of success, facilities, administrative support and promotion); and Outputs (publications, research quality and reputation). UFSC stood out in Inputs, with a grade 57.5 (out of 100), following Universidade Estadual Paulista (Unesp), ranked 2nd among Brazilian institutions in this area.

The interdisciplinary approach evaluated by the ranking is a growing trend, seen as a solution to complex problems that require the integration of different academic perspectives.

Visit the [THE website](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/interdisciplinary-science-rankings#!/length/25/sort_by/scores_overall/sort_order/asc) to find out more about the ranking and the position of the participating univeristies.

Access [here](https://www.timeshighereducation.com/world-university-rankings/interdisciplinary-science-rankings-2025-methodology?utm_source=ranking&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=isr&utm_content=embargo&spMailingID=30178206&spUserID=MTc4NDU1ODQ2MzI5MQS2&spJobID=2591149595&spReportId=MjU5MTE0OTU5NQS2) the methodology of the THE Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2025.

## [UFSC is among the 10 best universities in the THE Latin America University Rankings 2024](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2024/11/12/ufsc-esta-entre-as-10-melhores-universidades-no-ranking-internacional-latin-america-university-rankings-2024-do-the/?lang=en)

![](http://sinter.paginas.ufsc.br/files/2024/11/THE-Master-Rankings_LATAM_2024_RGB_COL-300x100.png)

The Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) occupies the 10th position in the Times Higher Education (THE) Latin America University Rankings 2024, moving up two positions from last year, when it was in the 12th position. With this new ranking, the institution is now one of the top 10 universities in Latin America.

![](http://sinter.paginas.ufsc.br/files/2020/09/the.png)USC is among the 5 best Brazilian federal universities in the THE World University Rankings 2024

## [UFSC is ranked 23rd best university in Latin America and The Caribbean by the QS](https://sinter.ufsc.br/2023/09/13/ufsc-e-classificada-como-23a-melhor-universidade-da-america-latina/?lang=en)

![](http://sinter.paginas.ufsc.br/files/2023/09/logo-qs-300x61.png)The results of the **QS World University Rankings: Latin America & The Caribbean 2024** were published on Wednesday, 13 September, and ranked the Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina (UFSC) among the 23 best universities in Latin America. UFSC occupies the **8th** position among the Brazilian universities and the **4th** among the federal education institutions in Brazil.

The ranking is produced annually by Quacquarelli Symonds (QS), a British company specialized in education. The ranking analyzed 430 institutions in 25 Latin American and Caribbean countries and at the top of the list is the Universidade de São Paulo (USP). The overall score of each institution is calculated using eight metrics, each with a different weight: Academic Reputation (30%); Employer Reputation (20%); Faculty Student Ratio (10%); Faculty Staff with PhD (10%); International Research Network (10%); Citations per Paper (10%); Papers per Faculty (5%) and Web Impact (5%). The strongest indicators for UFSC in this edition were Faculty Staff with PhD (99.7 score), International Research Network (98.1 score) and Web Impact (97.4 score).

In terms of UFSC articles and external citations between 2017 and 2022, the main theme for UFSC was studies in the **Life Sciences & Medicine** areas.

Check out the complete ranking results [here](https://www.topuniversities.com/latin-america-caribbean-overall?&page=0).

- **SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-Being:** ranked 201-300 overall, among 1,788 universities assessed, with a score of 66.4;
- **SDG 7 – Affordable and Clean Energy:** ranked 201-300 overall, among 1,181 universities assessed, with a score of 58.2;
- **SDG 17 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions (SDG 16):** ranked 301-400 overall, among 1,256 institutions assessed, with a score of 59.1.

UFSC also stood out in SDG 6 (Clean water and sanitation), SGD 9 (Industry, innovation and infrastructure), and SDG 12 (Responsible consumption and production).

**About THE and the Impact Rankings**

Times Higher Education (THE) is a British magazine that publishes news and articles on higher education and annually produces a set of rankings considered among the most comprehensive, balanced and reliable in the world. In addition to the institutional actions related to the SDGs, THE also ranks institutions based on the research conducted for each goal.

The *Impact Rankings* specifically highlight universities that stand out in relation to the United Nations SDGs, not only in individual areas but also in their overall contribution to sustainable global development. By excelling in a variety of SDGs, these universities showcase their commitment to addressing the world’s most pressing challenges, including environmental sustainability, social inclusion and economic growth.

For more information, visit the website: [www.timeshighereducation.com/impactrankings](http://www.timeshighereducation.com/impactrankings)

### [**Tarlac Agricultural University**](https://www.facebook.com/tarlacagriculturaluniversity/)

[23. Juni](https://www.facebook.com/tarlacagriculturaluniversity/posts/pfbid0888ZzoumnHqa65Lm26auEwoEszhfvnwQaWZyssBpZ9BdU4b1MdYrHgbcTYWtjLgEl)  · ![Mit Public geteilt](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

𝐐𝐔𝐎𝐓𝐄𝐃 𝐛𝐲 𝐈𝐧𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐔𝐧𝐢𝐭

Upon receiving this year’s Times Higher Education (THE) Sustainability Impact Ratings results in Jakarta, Indonesia, where Tarlac Agricultural University (TAU) maintained its 1001-1500 ranking, Dr. Silverio Ramon DC. Salunson, TAU President, expresses his sincere appreciation for the entire TAU community. He highlights that the contributions of every TAUian ultimately center on serving people, rising above the mere pursuit of institutional rankings. He reiterates the University's firm pledge to intensify its efforts in food security and sustainable agriculture, to safeguard vital ecosystems, and to advocate for inclusive policies that uplift all sectors.

While he candidly recognizes the areas where TAU needs further development, he emphasizes that these gaps represent valuable opportunities for learning, innovation, and improved service rather than serving as permanent setbacks.

Most importantly, President Salunson stresses the University's profound commitment to its core values of Resilience, Agility, Innovation, Sustainability, and Excellence. He further notes that the RAISE brand is a genuine promise to upcoming generations, not just a slogan; a practical approach to solving real-world problems, not a passing trend; and an ongoing, collective journey that is measured one Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) at a time.

# [2403.18140] Juru: Legal Brazilian Large Language Model from Reputable Sources

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.18140) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.18140v2)
> Abstract:The high compute cost associated with pretraining large language models limits their research. Two strategies have emerged to address this issue: domain specialization and pretraining with high-quality data. To explore these strategies, we specialized the Mistral-7B model with 1.9 billion unique tokens from reputable Brazilian legal sources and conducted few-shot evaluations on legal and general knowledge test suites. Our model, Juru, demonstrates the benefits of domain specialization by achieving improved performance on legal benchmarks, even with a reduced amount of pretraining data. However, this domain specialization through continued pretraining comes at the cost of increased forgetting in unrelated domains, as evidenced by performance degradation on general knowledge test suites in both Portuguese and English. This study contributes to the growing body of scientific evidence showing that pretraining data selection may enhance the performance of large language models, enabling the exploration of these models at a lower cost. Juru is publicly available at [this https URL](https://huggingface.co/roseval/Juru-7B) .
